question: The harmonic mean of a collection of numbers is the reciprocal of the arithmetic mean of the reciprocals of the numbers in the collection. For example, the harmonic mean of \(4,\) \(4,\) and \(5\) is \[\frac{1}{\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{5}\right)} = \frac{30}{7}.\] What is the harmonic mean of all the real roots of the \(4050\)th degree polynomial \[ \begin{aligned} &\small \prod_{k=1}^{2025}(kx^2 - 4x - 3) \\ &= (x^2 - 4x - 3) \\ &\quad {}\cdot (2x^2 - 4x - 3) \\ &\quad {}\cdot (3x^2 - 4x - 3)\cdots \\ &\quad (2025x^2 - 4x - 3)? \end{aligned} \]
solution:
Group the roots by their quadratic factors. For each pair, Vieta’s formulas let us find the sum of the reciprocals without finding the roots themselves.

For every \(k\geq 1\), the discriminant of \(kx^2-4x-3\) is
\[
16+12k>0,
\]
so each factor has two distinct real roots. Neither root is zero. Also, if a number \(r\) were a root of factors with indices \(k\) and \(\ell\), subtracting their equations would give \((k-\ell)r^2=0\). Since \(r\neq 0\), this forces \(k=\ell\). Thus the product has \(4050\) distinct nonzero real roots.

Let \(a_k,b_k\) be the roots of the \(k\)th factor. Vieta’s formulas give
\[
a_k+b_k=\frac{4}{k},
\qquad a_kb_k=-\frac{3}{k}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{1}{a_k}+\frac{1}{b_k}
=\frac{a_k+b_k}{a_kb_k}
=\frac{4/k}{-3/k}
=-\frac{4}{3}.
\]
The arithmetic mean of all the reciprocals is therefore
\[
\frac{2025\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right)}{4050}
=-\frac{2}{3}.
\]
Taking its reciprocal gives the harmonic mean \(\boxed{-\frac{3}{2}}\), choice B.
